For what I like, I would have probably given 3 stars, but I want to review these paint markers for what they are. Personally the paint inside isn’t up to my standards, but considering the price and the amount of markers, in addition to a case, they’re what I expected.

First, they come in a zippered case which I prefer over a cardboard box, which I wish more companies would do. Each marker has its own slot and the inserts are removable. It also comes with a printed swatch chart and extra nibs. Some of the swatches are pretty close, some are not, so you’ll want to make your own. The chart has names and numbers, but there’s no markings on the paint pens themselves - kinda pointless and you have to just go by the cap color. As long as you have a chart and keep them in order I guess it’s not that bad, but what if you take multiple out or use different storage? When swatching them, I noticed that some are nice and “juicy” where the paint flows nicely, but others are dryer, and you’ll need to go slower to get better coverage. The paint is on the thinner side, so they can get a little streaky, and the opacity just isn’t there. The dark colors are obviously better, but mid tones (like red) didn’t cover black ink, even with three coats, and some of the dark colors (like dark green) failed here, too. Personally, I prefer opaque paint, but this might not be a negative for some. Of the colors, I do think there’s a nice selection of warm, cool, a couple of skin tone, and neutral colors, and even a handful of metallic. For a beginner set, I think there’s colors are good to get started for sure.

I plan to play around with them a little more, but I think this set will get passed along to the kids for their projects and play. For the current price, they’re worth checking out, and would make a good gift for kids. If you are familiar with some of the more expensive brands of paint markers though, I would probably skip these. It just depends on what you want them for.

The brush tips feel springy and make thin outlines or solid fills without fighting me. Coverage is strong. On paper and canvas I get crisp lines in 1 coat. Once fully dry on the rocks and mug it held up to a rinse in cool water.

For the size of the set and how reliably these write, the value feels excellent. Easy start, bright results, and dependable control across materials. I reach for them now when I want paint look with marker speed.

I’m absolutely in love with these markers! I recently had the chance to use them for some artwork (I'll be sharing pictures soon), and they completely exceeded my expectations in every way. From the moment I opened the set, I was impressed with the vibrant color selection. With 80 shades to choose from, there’s a perfect hue for any project, whether you're looking for something bold and eye-catching or soft and subtle. Additionally, the dual-tipped design provides incredible versatility, enabling you to work with greater precision on fine details or cover larger areas with ease, depending on the project or surface you’re working on.

The paint itself flows beautifully—smooth and consistent. I’ve worked with other paint markers before, but these have an especially nice texture. The colors layer effortlessly on top of one another, giving you the ability to create depth and dimension in your artwork. I've used these on a variety of surfaces, including canvas, rocks, wood, and even fabric, and the results have been consistently fantastic. The markers perform well on each material, with no bleeding or fading, and the color payoff is rich and true to the cap’s shade.

The quality of the markers feels top-notch, which is something I really appreciate. They have a premium, well-constructed feel, and yet they’re surprisingly beginner-friendly. You don’t need to be a professional artist to get good results with these, but even as someone who has experience with more advanced projects, I found them incredibly fun and easy to use. Most of the colors have great opacity, even on darker surfaces, and the blending ability is better than I anticipated, especially for acrylic markers. It’s easy to mix and layer colors without them becoming muddy or streaky, which makes a huge difference when you’re trying to achieve smooth transitions or soft gradients in your art.

Another thing I really love is how well the tips hold their shape. I’ve had markers in the past where the tips lose their form after only a few uses, but these maintain their point for precision and offer smooth, even coverage every time. I’ve also noticed no issues with drying out or skipping, which can be a problem with cheaper markers. I’ve been able to work for extended periods without needing to shake or prime the pens, which is a huge plus when you’re in the zone.

Now, I do have a tiny complaint, but it’s really nothing major. A few of the darker colors, especially the deep reds and blacks, can bleed a little when you’re using them on thinner paper. However, this is pretty common with highly pigmented acrylic markers, so it wasn’t a dealbreaker for me. It’s just something to keep in mind if you plan on using them for detailed line work on thin paper—especially if you're working with delicate materials or want to avoid any bleed-through.

All in all, I’m beyond pleased with these markers, and I’m giving them a solid 5 stars. They’ve been a fantastic addition to my art supplies, and I know I’ll be reaching for them again and again in the future. Since I enjoy all kinds of crafts and have crafty kids, I was excited to try this set of acrylic markers from Artecho. To summarize, I think it is a decent value for mixed-media use, especially for use with kids. However, a lack of quality control and many similar colors may not satisfy an adult artist.

Pros: I have used many types of non-toxic and paint markers in the past on a variety of mediums, and was thrilled to receive 72 colors in this set. The brush heads are smooth and a delight to work with. The fine tips most resemble traditional press-down paint marker tips, though you don't have to press these down to work - a real improvement! The rainbow of colors is very attractive in the protective, easy-to-transport case. All markers can be easily accessed when the case is open.

Now for the drawbacks. Some of the paints look best on shiny surfaces, but tend to rub off when touched, even after drying. Once fully dried, the acrylic has the best staying-power on matte surfaces without using a fixative. Some of the colors are really beautiful and smooth ("carmine", "sapphire"). Others are weakly pigmented or look muddy ("watermelon", "emerald"). The weak pigments don’t cover darker surfaces or lines, so beware if you’re trying to layer. I was super disappointed at the noticeable difference between the color of the brush and fine tip on many of the markers. See the picture of the color chart: the upper half of each box is the brush side, and the lower half of the box is the fine tip. In most cases, the brush color was quite a bit more pigmented and vibrant than the fine tip color. This difference means I cannot switch between tip types and expect my work to look consistent.

The numbering system and color names seem illogical, and the markers are not organized in the case according to either the numbering or the color chart. Many of the names inadequately reflect the actual color; for example, "brown" is a light pink, and "indigo" is a greenish gray. "Blackberry" and "crimson" are both pale pink. In fact, 18 of the markers are pink tones, including "beige", "camel", and "earth red", and similar in appearance. As the paints are not true to the color of their lids, it is hard to find particular shades unless you rearrange them and use a color chart. However, the included chart lists 120 colors, and there are only 72 in this set, leaving many blank boxes. The color chart is also printed on shiny paper, so the colors tend to smear.

Overall, I think the value of this introductory set is fine at its current price point (24 u.s.d. at the time of review). The markers will be good for painting on stones, wood, and other mixed media crafts with kids (especially kids who like pink), and I think they'll hold up through multiple projects. However, if you're a serious artist or looking to add to your existing stock of acrylic markers, I don't recommend this set from Artecho.

I have been using old-school, strong-smelling, quick-to-dry-out paint pens for many years, but when I saw these WUO acrylic paint markers that didn’t require pressing and holding, I had to try them. What I wasn’t expecting was how much better they would be.

* Color Range & Appearance: I went with the 60-color set, and I’m glad I did. The colors cover a nice spectrum, including a few pale shades that don’t look obvious from the pen exteriors. For example, the pens made me think there was no pale green, but once tested, there were actually a couple of lighter greens. I’d still love to see extra black, white, gold, and silver included, since those get used up quickly.

* Application & Coverage: The paint goes on somewhat thin (not thick and globby), which turns out to be a strength. It allows layering and blending instead of clumping or streaking. On paper, the coverage is smooth and much nicer than regular markers. On ceramics, you’ll likely need more than one coat like I did. They also work over other acrylic paints (a little tougher on ones that dry glossy, I found), but I find they perform best directly on unfinished ceramic surfaces.

* Packaging & Storage: The set comes in stackable plastic trays that look neat and high-end. Each tray snaps securely into the one below it: tilt the back down first, then lower the front, and finally lock it with the white toggle on the front. I really like this design for keeping them organized.

* Extras: There are tester cards so you can preview how each color looks on black and white paper, plus some small project ideas. One even involves painting onto a sponge, adding water, and watching it puff up, which was fun.

* Odor & Safety: Unlike traditional paint pens, these have no odor at all, which surprised me. That makes them much more pleasant to use and safe for children, though you’d still want to be careful about clothing and surfaces.

* Use Case: I definitely plan to use these for craft projects, but I'm thinking that I'll also use them for detail work on larger acrylic canvas paintings that I do. They shake easily to refresh the paint flow when needed, and I haven’t had issues with clogging. Just avoid pressing too hard on the tips since that could damage them.

* Wishlist for Improvement:
⦁ Pen exterior colors don’t always match the actual paint shade.
⦁ Include more duplicate “workhorse” colors (black, white, gold, silver).
⦁ Offer a fine liner option (about half the tip width) for super-detailed work.

* Value for the Cost: At 39.99 at the time I'm writing this, that's not cheap for a set of craft pens. But, this is a really large set and if  you were to buy each pen individually you would pay much more. Plus you're getting craft projects to go with it. So, all in all, I think this is an exceptional value for the cost...which I hope doesn't change.

* Bottom Line: These paint pens exceeded my expectations. The colors are vibrant, the pens layer and blend well, they store easily, and best of all, they’re odor-free. They make me want to reach for them instead of my old paint pens. Super highly recommended. Go for the kit of 60 if you regularly do crafts and/or use acrylic paints.

This TECADA 168 Colors Acrylic Paint Brush Markers is a weird mix of really good and really not good. I am a professional artist, and I own thousands of acrylic markers, to be able to compare to. The first red flag I see is that the name is Tecada, but the item I received is called Flysea markers. They use the exact same box as a ton of other Chinese paint markers, and the same random extremely unhelpful number system. I was quite worried this would just be a duplicate of other sets I have.The next red flag is that these markers are brand new, but already the numbers - the literal only way to distinguish each marker from each other - are half wiped off. That has already rendered some of them virtually impossible to use.I was fortunate to receive all the markers in the box, and for the most part they are all distinct colors. The box is not good though - competing brands include a zip case organizer with elastic strap loops, and that is far more worth one's money, to be able to keep these in the color order you need them - but good luck taking the time to re-sort all 168 by color order. Moreover, the color swatch on the bottom of the box, is not covered by anything, so all the swatches (this not being real acrylic which is plastic, but some cheap craft gouache) have mostly scraped off within a week from just gently moving the box around.Some of these are actually very decently pigmented, more than other brands, which was a pleasant shock. Most have low opacity though, and you'll be using a lot of layers for a long time spent, if you actually want to color over anything completely. This is more of a layering marker. I was also pleased that generally speaking, these are not an exact match to my other sets - even those with essentially the same box and unmarked markers. They do NOT say Guangna, which is great, because nearly all of this type when you buy them under whatever random name, what you receive is a marker that says GuangNa on the side, and those are both very translucent, and also often very repetitive. These are no-name.Another major good point was that these are as waterproof as POSCA or other similar markers... which is to say, mostly. They, like those, can have a slight bleed with certain colors, or other paints.The best part of this set is that the color swatches are arranged by color, even though the numbers make no sense. That is the one thing that makes this the most usable.The color range is decent, with a few actual dark colors, and a few more realistic greens than most have. This set does not have any actual dark brown - only very chalky browns - and it does not have enough reds. There is not 1 single actual orange in the whole set. Don't buy this looking for orange.Overall, this is a hit and miss set, that for what it offers seems way overpriced to me. When ordered, it was a whopping $77. But I personally would not pay more than maybe $45, given the tons of competing markers on the market. But this really all depends on what you are expecting to do with this. If you need it to be opaque, look elsewhere. If you want layering, and a new range of colors, with some actual darks, this may be a good addition to your collection. I really liked some of the unusual colors provided, that are unlike those in other sets - some more complex grays, a deep red and green, a decent yellow range.For me personally, I would never recommend buying this to anyone, until they fix the markers so the number labeling actually STAYS on the marker. They, and all the time you spent coloring in the swatches - are absolutely useless if you cannot identify any of the markers. If not, that would transform this to a set only useful for 6 year olds. And who is going to spend $77 on a set of markers for 6 year olds? Not me. That price is for people who are actually serious about their coloring, and who are at the least serious crafters, if not semi-pro artists.This set is very low quality, mixed with some random high quality elements, and some well-pigmented colors.

I have the smaller 36 pack of dual Grabie markers, so when I saw they had come out with a larger pack, I grabbed them up.:)

They are the same size and quality as the smaller pack, although the coloring on the marker packaging is different (relief). They also seem to have gone through a color name and number change for some of the colors that were included in the 36; you'll find most of the 36 pack here (with some that look slightly different). This pack covers a wide variety of colors, and there weren't really any (for this coloring anyways) that I was wishing were included.

I absolutely love that these don't have to be primed, and they have brush tips instead of hard nibs. The downside is that if you aren't careful (and honestly, even if you are), the tips of the brushes can break down farely quickly, which makes more detailed work very hard. They can also get bits of dried paint on them, so be prepared to pick the little bits off.
As of writing this, I don't think Grabie offers replacement tips, but I believe they are pretty similar to another brands brush tips, that you can buy replacements for, fairly cheap.

The really lovely thing about these is that they don't bleed through (like some acrylics have separation liquid that leaks through). You can easily color a double sided page, and have zero issues come through the back (given your paper quality, super thin types might show through, I'm unsure).

There's mutliple ways to use these; on rocks, glass paper, vinyl, plastic, etc (given you have a sealant) and I'm still finding extra uses for them, like adding details to coloring pages, or fixing some art when I've gone outside the lines with the medium I'm using, or even to bring back the original color on clay that's darkened too much.

They're very opaque, so you do need to be careful when coloring in pages; you'll want to have a fineliner ready to go over lines if you color over, as these will either soften the lines, or completely wipe them out. You need to be slow while coloring portions in, because if you are fast, you'll get streaks or blotches in the paint (like some areas of my coloring page; book is A Million Kittens). Do make sure to shake them prior to using to blend them.

My main gripe is that they really downgraded on the carry case packaging. I love the 36 pack case; it's softer plastic and textured, with no sharp edges, and it's easy to pull the markers out (and put them back).
With this larger pack, the packaging is a thicker, cheaper plastic that I can't get the markers out, or put them away, without scraping my hands up from the sharp opening. It can be frustrating. I really wish they'd stayed with the same packaging.

I do really like these and they've gone into my travel art bag. My original pack has yet to run out of ink, so they seem like they last a good bit. I'll have to report back if/when they do.

I love paint markers. I'm not sure there's an entirely logical process here... I don't use them anywhere near as much as I should given how many I've gotten, but I identified as an artist in my youth, and having fun art supplies readily available is a lot like breathing fresh air for me.I have ordered at least a half dozen paint marker packs through Vine, including several other sets from GuangNa. Generally, they earn 4 stars from me. I have been very frustrated by their lack of true green shades in their other sets. This set covers it. Wow, does it cover it.Some things you should know if you get this: Numbers are in the 600s, 700s, and 800s. For numbers that could be easily confused, they put a small dot in the upper left to indicate the top of the number. I show this in my video.For filling in your own color card, the row closest to it was almost entirely the left side, and you gradually move right as you go through each row. There are exceptions, but this helped me save time searching for the correct square once I realized.You may note the colors are not exact matches of the printed colors in many cases. I don't know why they don't make a color card and take a picture of it, but this discrepancy has been very normal with already primed paint markers.These acrylic paint markers come primed. You do not need to shake/press to prepare them for use, and these are much easier to control than the kinds that require priming. However, these are also more matte in appearance when dried and relatively easy to scratch. Plan to use a sealant or similar to protect your paintings done with these markers. It's a question of trade-offs. I prefer the ease of use these provide even knowing more work is necessary to protect my creations. You may not.Regardless, I'm thrilled with the color selection of these markers. I can't wait to do more with them!

I picked up the Grabie Acrylic Paint Pens hoping for a no-fuss way to add detail to my seasonal crafts and DIY projects—and these markers delivered. The 0.7 mm extra fine tips are ideal for outlining, lettering, and adding crisp accents, especially on textured surfaces like wood, stone, and canvas. Great ink/paint quality & rather easy to use. Just need a bit or patience to get them all primed. Pros:• Vibrant Colors: All 18 shades pop beautifully• Extra Fine Tip: The 0.7 mm nib is perfect for detail work, outlining, and labeling.• Multi-Surface Friendly: Works well on wood, glass, metal, plastic, stone, and canvas.• Quick-Drying & Low Odor: Great for indoor use—no strong fumes or long wait times.• Senior-Friendly Grip: Comfortable to hold, even for shaky hands or longer sessions.Cons:• Initial Priming Takes Patience: You’ll need to press the tip a few times to get the ink flowing.• Not Waterproof: Best for indoor projects or sealed surfaces—rain will wash it away.• Cap Colors ≠ Ink Colors: Double-check before using; some caps are misleading.Pro Tip:  I read that it is important to keep the cap on when shaking but I don’t always follow instructions, just ask my hubby! Anyway, I have a lovely blue streak on my hobby table. Lesson learned!Recommended whether you're labeling garden stakes, decorating ornaments, or personalizing pet gear, these pens glide smoothly and dry fast without smudging. Drawing pad is included in the carry case.

The Grabie Acrylic Paint Pens 18 pack are absolutely fantastic for both beginners and experienced artists! I’ve used them on a variety of surfaces — wood, rocks, glass, metal, plastic, canvas, and even fabric — and the coverage and color vibrancy are consistently excellent.  Each pen has a smooth, fine point tip that allows for precise detailing and clean lines, which makes them perfect for outlining, lettering, or adding intricate designs. The flow of paint is steady and even — no blotching or skipping — and the colors are rich, opaque, and quick-drying.  The 18 pack color selection. is beautiful, with a good balance of bright tones and neutral shades. All of the colors layer nicely when dry. I also appreciate that they don’t have a strong chemical smell like some other paint pens.  The acrylic ink quality is top-notch as it’s permanent once dry, waterproof, and resistant to fading or scratching. I’ve made several painted rocks and decorated mugs, and the designs have held up perfectly over time. The pens are also easy to activate: just shake, press the tip a few times, and the ink starts flowing smoothly.  I also love that the set comes well-packaged, with each pen clearly labeled and capped tightly to prevent drying out. The pens are comfortable to hold, lightweight, and the fine tips haven’t frayed or clogged even after multiple uses.  Cleanup is minimal — the paint dries fast, and there’s no smudging or bleeding. For crafts, journaling, DIY gifts, or detailed artwork, these pens are incredibly versatile and reliable.  Overall, the Grabie Acrylic Paint Pens deliver professional-level results at a great price. They’re vibrant, precise, long-lasting, and fun to use on almost any surface. Highly recommend for anyone who loves art, crafting, or adding a creative touch to everyday items!
